body: In the 1960s, Neptune posed a **propellant** problem: a direct flight could take thirty years. Yet Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune approached a **configuration**, an **alignment** recurring every 175 years. A launch window could **stitch** their encounters into a **unified** **itinerary**. Grand Tour **reconnaissance** through successive **flybys** could reduce flight time, **launcher** requirements and **expenditure**. Computation made the geometry **usable**. At JPL, Michael Minovitch developed **ballistic** **multi-planet** paths; in 1965 Gary Flandro mapped the outer-planet **opportunity**. The manoeuvre had an older **pedigree**; NASA calls its origins **unsettled**, so singular **authorship** misleads. Those contributions turned a **fleeting** **celestial** configuration into mission design, each encounter making the next world **attainable**. Near a planet, a craft follows a **hyperbola**. Speed gained **inbound** is lost **outbound**, a **reciprocal** pattern in the planet's **co-moving** frame. Yet gravity **swivels** its velocity **vector**. In the **heliocentric** frame, adding planetary orbital velocity to that vector changes the craft's **kinetic** energy. Momentum changes hands; the planet's response is **imperceptible**. Voyager 2 left Earth in 1977. Jupiter in 1979 **reoriented** it toward Saturn; Saturn in 1981 bent it toward Uranus; Uranus in 1986 sent it toward Neptune in 1989. Each **approach** required precise **targeting** at a prescribed **epoch**. A course **adjustment** could shift **downstream** geometry years later. The four **waypoints** formed one **interdependent** **cascade**, not a **piecemeal** itinerary. Gravity assist is no **perpetual-motion** trick. Passing behind a moving planet can **augment** Sun-relative speed; passing ahead can **decelerate** it. **Conservation** holds: the planet **cedes** or receives a **minuscule** share of orbital energy. Rockets still handled launch and **trim** burns; Voyager's **limitation** became an **asset** because its route itself supplied **propulsion**.
